body:
Parent: #1794. Design: #4975.

## Scope — transport + CLI/REPL
Implement a user-initiated, single-file copy from one running `id` server to another. Keep the source unchanged. Use a server-side transfer module with one small interface shared by the CLI/REPL and the later web adapter.

- The CLI/REPL command addresses a source server, a stored source name, a destination node ID, and an optional destination name. The source server performs the transfer; the local CLI client key must not be mistaken for the source server identity.
- Reuse Iroh `BLOBS_ALPN` for content-addressed bytes and the existing `/iroh-meta/3` metadata path to register the destination name. Do not put file bytes on `/id-world/1`, the world outbox, or through a browser.
- Keep the source and destination names explicit. Default to refusing an existing destination name; replacement must be an explicit user choice and preserve the existing file via the file-store archive behavior.
- Authorize the initiating user at the source before reading/sending the named file. The destination applies its existing write policy to the authenticated source-server node ID. World membership/capabilities alone do not grant file access.
- Transfer the complete blob before registering the name; report success only after destination registration confirms the blob. Interrupted sends must not create a visible dangling name. Repeating the same transfer should be safe/idempotent; never delete the source as part of send.
- Apply the existing listing metadata contract from #4973/#5191: the destination records the authenticated sending node as the new copy's origin and its first-write time as `created`/uploaded time. Do not claim that the origin tag is a signed attestation.

## Out of scope
Web UI (tracked separately); directories/batches; move/delete-source semantics; a new transport channel; changes to #1793's tag/petname scope.

## Parent acceptance criteria (verbatim from #1794)
- A file can be sent from one running server to another by a user action in CLI/REPL and in web (or the unsupported surfaces are explicitly scoped out with reasons).
- The transfer is covered by an integration test or a documented two-server probe.

## Done check
A two-Iroh-node test or documented probe proves authorized CLI/REPL transfer, destination contents/name and origin metadata, denied unallowlisted destination, no visible name after interruption, conflict behavior, and safe retry. CLI and REPL use the same server-side transfer interface.

## Ordering
This is the first implementation slice. The web adapter issue depends on this transfer module and protocol being available.
